Gene Description

DDX3X is a DEAD-box RNA helicase that binds RNA and uses an ATP-dependent cycle to remodel short RNA duplexes. It promotes translation of selected mRNAs and supports formation of functional 80S initiation complexes through interactions with translation-initiation machinery. DDX3X also performs separable noncatalytic signaling roles: it helps recruit IRF3 to IKKε during antiviral interferon induction and stimulates casein kinase 1 in Wnt signaling. The protein shuttles between nucleus and cytoplasm and can enter stress granules and other conditional assemblies. Its cellular effects depend on transcript, stimulus and cell type. Pathogenic DDX3X variants are associated with neurodevelopmental disease.

Summary: DDX3X contributes to cytoplasmic antiviral receptor signaling through the IKKε–IRF3 module.

Suggested Questions for Experts

Q: Which RNA substrates and assay conditions explain the reported DNA unwinding and RNA annealing activities, and can the DNA result be independently reproduced given the 2026 correction and incomplete original data?

Q: Does DDX3X directly contact poly(A) tails in the export mRNP experiments, or do the observations reflect contact with other portions of polyadenylated transcripts?

Q: Which activities and cellular distributions distinguish the naturally occurring 646-residue product from the 662-residue product?

Q: Which molecular steps connect DDX3X to intrinsic apoptosis, mitochondrial translation and cadherin-associated neighborhoods in the source-specific contexts where those assignments remain uncertain?

Suggested Experiments

Experiment: Compare sequence-verified 662- and 646-residue products in matched RNA binding/unwinding, initiation-complex reconstitution and signaling assays, with expression and folding controls.

Experiment: Retest DNA unwinding with matched 5′- and 3′-tailed duplexes, tag-cleaved preparations and orthogonal product detection; separately test target-specific RNA annealing and poly(A)-tail contact.

📚 Additional Documentation

Notes

(DDX3X-notes.md)

DDX3X biological notes

DDX3X couples RNA recognition and ATP hydrolysis to remodeling of short RNA duplexes. Human full-length protein and engineered catalytic fragments have been tested, but fragment activity does not establish the function of the naturally shorter product. The 2011 biochemical article has a 2026 correction that resolves several presentation errors while leaving specified original images and quantitative data unavailable; independently corroborated RNA chemistry remains central, and its substrate-dependent DNA result remains non-core with that limitation explicit. PMID:21589879(https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21589879/), PMID:29037760(https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29037760/), PMID:31300642(https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31300642/), PMID:41587182(https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41587182/).

An auxiliary translation-initiation role complements RNA helicase activity. DDX3X supports joining of mature subunits into functional 80S complexes, associates with initiation factors, and regulates selected structured transcripts. RNA dependence differs among the associations; effects on cyclin E1, ATF4 and growth are conditional and need not be uniform across cell types. PMID:22323517(https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22323517/), PMID:20837705(https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20837705/), PMID:29062139(https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29062139/).

Two signaling activities are mechanistically separable from RNA catalysis. DDX3X helps recruit IRF3 to IKKε during antiviral signaling, and it stimulates CK1 in Wnt signaling. The IRF3-recruitment mutant evidence and purified CK1 assays support these roles without assigning kinase activity to DDX3X, an experimentally resolved higher-order kinase architecture or a universal dependence on helicase activity. PMID:23478265(https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23478265/), PMID:29222110(https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29222110/), PMID:23413191(https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23413191/).

DDX3X shuttles between nucleus and cytoplasm, associates with translating particles and can enter stress granules. Cytosol/nucleoplasm observations refine broad locations; a peripheral 40S association does not make it a permanent ribosomal protein. Granule, exosome and mitochondrial observations describe distinct contexts rather than an exclusive compartment or extracellular catalytic function. PMID:15507209(https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15507209/), PMID:18596238(https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18596238/), PMID:28733330(https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28733330/), PMID:28869602(https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28869602/).

Mouse macrophage knockout/rescue and NLRP3-association experiments support a conserved contextual inflammasome role. The human ortholog inferences preserve species and construct limits. Poly(A)-tail contact, source-specific annealing, cadherin binding, two intrinsic-apoptosis assignments and the source-specific membrane/HCV-network observations remain unresolved where the necessary assays could not be independently adjudicated. Uncertainty preserves curator evidence and is not a negative biological assertion. PMID:31511697(https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31511697/), PMID:27546789(https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27546789/), PMID:25468996(https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25468996/), PMID:21883093(https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21883093/), PMID:16301996(https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/16301996/).

The official products contain 662 and 646 residues. The shorter sequence replaces canonical residues 35–51 with a serine. No inspected experiment establishes identical activity or inactivity of that natural product; the 132–607, 168–582 and other laboratory fragments are separate constructs. Disease-variant reporter phenotypes likewise do not establish one universal gain-of-function mechanism. PMID:31300642(https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31300642/), PMID:20862261(https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20862261/), PMID:26235985(https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26235985/).

Positive generic binding assertions are retained as contextual when a specific partner class or mechanism cannot be justified. Supported class refinements do not imply that DDX3X activates the partner, performs its catalysis, or binds every site of a full-length product. This follows the current project annotation policy. No NEW row is proposed: the four core activities and their supported processes are already represented, and the two inspected GO-CAM models already encode the signaling-adaptor role.

Genuine Falcon authentication and configured fallback quota failures prevented a provider report; manual source research was performed instead. Original source records, publication caches and official product metadata remain unchanged. Access distinctions, literal provenance and assay limits are recorded in the evidence guide and primary-source notes.

The broad innate immune-response observation is retained as contextual: pattern-recognition signaling and regulation of interferon production do not logically entail GO:0045087 through current is_a/part_of ancestry. The source retains its positive TBK1/IRF3 response evidence. PMID:18583960(https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18583960/).

Follow-up evidence and term specificity — 2026-10-17

The auxiliary initiation-factor core is supported by the purified-component 80S experiment in PMID:22323517(https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3367175/), Figure 7F–G, in addition to depletion and association experiments. GO:0003743 describes function in initiation; the demonstrated assembly contribution fits that definition. ATPase dependence and a molecular bridge remain hypotheses for this step. The complete bounded comparator query includes initiation-factor annotations for EIF5B and EIF4A1 but none for DHX29 or DHX33; that mixed convention is disclosed and does not justify adding an annotation merely to fill a gap.

The plasma-membrane assertion is retained contextually using independent human-cell imaging in PMID:29899501(https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5998047/), with the original PMID:23413191 localization assay still unrecovered. The positive CAP-Rf reporter endpoint in PMID:10074132(https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC104042/) retains its unresolved causal stage; the NAS cyclin-E1 summary in PMID:22492871(https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3387391/) is refined using established translation regulation. These judgments preserve the distinct source claims.

The current is_a/part_of graph confirms GO:0002753 → GO:0002221 → GO:0002758, but does not connect those terms to GO:0045087 by the proposed final edge. GO:0002758 directly inherits from GO:0002218 and GO:0002757. Regulation of an innate response is not substituted for the response itself; the experimentally supported TBK1/IRF3 context remains non-core PMID:18583960(https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18583960/).

CSB/ERCC6 and DHX33 associations are refined to ATPase binding on their established enzymatic class, preserving reciprocal co-immunoprecipitation and RNA-dependence limits PMID:26030138(https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4451243/), PMID:26100019(https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4525307/). This does not require DDX3X to activate the partner. Forty-five prior general terms now use MODIFY with already supported specific replacements, as the project instructions require. All 207 guide decisions and replacements were cross-checked against the final review; source identities, qualifiers, products and the 2011-paper correction assessment are preserved.

Source-specific localization refinement

Nuclear-pore association and nuclear speckles are retained as distinct observations: the complete abstracts of PMID:15507209 and PMID:10329544 explicitly identify these locations. The latter also describes HCV-core-associated perinuclear redistribution. The compartment replacements preserve these observations rather than substituting nucleoplasm or cytosol alone; they do not assert exclusive residence or constitutive pore membership.

The diffuse cytoplasmic pool remains alongside condition-dependent stress granules in the evidence from PMID:18596238, PMID:21883093, PMID:29062139 (Results and Figure 1C) and PMID:24965446 (Results and Figure 3B). PMID:21883093 explicitly excludes processing bodies, and the DCP1a observations in PMID:24965446 are not transferred to DDX3. Endogenous DDX3X at the leading edge of spreading MRC5 fibroblasts is preserved separately from soluble cytosol (PMID:28733330, fractionation Results and Figure 4). Cell leading edge is not a typed descendant of cytoplasm in the inspected current ontology; the two replacements express complementary observed locations.

MAVS/IPS-1-associated mitochondrial proximity and HCV-associated lipid-droplet proximity remain qualified observations (PMID:20127681; PMID:21170385, Figures 6–7), not evidence of matrix import or of a particular membrane face. No new localization assertion is inferred from generic stress-granule background or from a partner's localization. These refinements change no action, imported source object, product, core function, or quotation.

Primary Source Notes

(DDX3X-primary-source-notes.md)

DDX3X primary-source notes

PMID:23478265, DOI 10.1128/MCB.01603-12, was independently inspected as indexed text from the author PDF. Methods use human full-length 662-aa DDX3X and engineered fragments, recombinant IKKε/IRF3, HEK293T/A549 cells and Sendai virus. Results/Figures 5–6 distinguish IKKε activation from IRF3 recruitment: “DDX3, but not the S102A mutant, interacts directly with IRF3.” The S102A mutant retains IKKε binding and activation but loses IRF3 association/phosphorylation and reporter enhancement; S102D supports the phosphorylation-dependent recruitment interpretation. The higher-order kinase arrangement in the final model is not an experimentally resolved architecture. No DDX3X kinase activity is inferred. The normal publication cache remains abstract-only; failed direct downloads and the successful indexed original access are both preserved.

PMID:29222110, original DOI 10.1242/jcs.207316, uses human DDX3X/CK1ε, a cytoplasmic FRET kinase sensor, DDX3X depletion, kinase inhibitors/dead-kinase controls, purified full-length protein and residues 414–582, and CK1-derived peptide assays. The Figure 3 caption supports the kinase-stimulation interpretation; its short exact quotation is attached to that activity in the review YAML. RNA inhibits the DDX3X–CK1 interaction/kinase stimulation, whereas CK1 phosphorylation reduces DDX3X ATPase activity in the tested system. Modeling of binding orientation is distinct from the ELISA, thermal-shift and biolayer-interferometry observations. Methods specify full-length protein purified from HEK293T cells and bacterial fragments; these constructs do not establish natural short-isoform functional equivalence.

PMID:23413191, DOI 10.1126/science.1231499, remains abstract-only after bounded publisher/supplement/repository attempts. Its actual abstract explicitly reports Wnt-dependent CK1ε binding/stimulation, Dishevelled phosphorylation, mammalian cells and Xenopus/Caenorhabditis developmental effects. This supports the established kinase-regulatory/Wnt function with the later mechanistic evidence, but does not recover its membrane-localization assay. The two signaling activities complement RNA helicase and auxiliary translation-initiation roles; they are not new annotation proposals because their specific MF/BP terms are already seeded.

RNA chemistry, translation and the 2026 correction

PMID:21589879(https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0017169), Methods (protein expression/purification and enzyme assays), Results and Figures 2–7, examines recombinant human full-length DDX3X, isolated domains and mutants. RNA unwinding, ATP hydrolysis and RNA-binding results support the helicase function. The positive DNA assay used an 18/38-nucleotide substrate with a 5′ extension; the tested 3′ extension did not support the same activity. An overhang preference does not establish processive directional translocation. The paper contains inconsistent numbering of its DADA substitution between sections; no unverified residue coordinate is asserted here.

PMID:41587182, editorial correction, complete correction text and revised figure captions, replaces the purification image in Figure 2A, clarifies TLC splices, corrects lane numbering and changes Figure 4F ordering. The notice reports that available original/repeat data support the explanations, but original images for Figures 2D, 3E, 4B–D, 4G–H, 6A–B and 7 and quantitative data for Figures 2–5 and 7 are unavailable. Thus resolved presentation corrections and unresolved data-verification limits must be distinguished. The article is not retracted and the notice does not explicitly reject unwinding. Independently supported RNA chemistry remains central; the source-specific DNA result is retained as non-core with an explicit verification limitation. The original publication cache remains unchanged. Figure captions and correction text were read; figure pixels and the correction’s underlying-data attachment were not independently inspected.

PMID:29037760(https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5693625/), Methods and biochemical Results, uses full-length tag-cleaved DDX3X and tests a 16-base-pair DNA duplex with a 25-nucleotide 3′ extension. The negative DNA result does not directly reproduce the earlier positive 5′-extended substrate. PMID:31300642(https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31300642/), structural and biochemical Methods/Results, instead uses an engineered human 132–607 core. Neither construct is the naturally shorter 646-residue product. DNA unwinding is therefore not a separate physiological core, and the two substrate conditions are preserved rather than presented as an exact replication conflict.

PMID:22323517(https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22323517/), interaction and translation-reconstitution Results/Methods, supports an auxiliary initiation-factor role and mature 80S joining. eIF2 association is RNA-dependent; eIF3 association survives RNA removal and is supported by purified-component experiments. Detection through eIF3C identifies the complex rather than an isolated eIF3C interface. Functional joining is demonstrated, while a specific bridging geometry and an ATPase requirement for that joining step are not established by this source. GO:0042256 includes joining mature ribosomal subunits; the annotation does not claim pre-rRNA biogenesis.

Source-specific unresolved assignments and contextual assemblies

PMID:18596238(https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18596238/), Figure 2C and mRNP-selection Methods, supports association with polyadenylated mRNPs but does not establish the poly(A) tail as the contact. The inspected Figure 5/RNase and fractionation results support a peripheral 40S association without making DDX3X a constitutive ribosomal protein. Complete original and supplementary coverage was not obtained. PMID:27546789(https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27546789/), RNA-compaction Results, supports DDX3X-dependent compaction; target-specific annealing remains unresolved because the necessary supplementary assay was not recovered. LAF-1 annealing cannot substitute for a DDX3X measurement.

PMID:25468996(https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4972397/), BioID Methods, uses E-cadherin–BirA in human MKN28 cells with control cells and perturbations. Proximity labeling does not by itself establish direct cadherin contact, and the DDX3X-specific supplementary target table was not recovered. PMID:16301996(https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/16301996/) distinguishes human carcinoma expression from mouse NIH-3T3 knockdown phenotypes; PMID:21883093(https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21883093/) supports stress-granule/apoptosis context. These accessible sources do not settle the specifically intrinsic apoptotic pathway. Their positive observations are retained; uncertainty does not assert absence of the function.

PMID:31511697(https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6980284/), NLRP3/ASC-speck Results and knockout/rescue/co-immunoprecipitation Methods, distinguishes mouse macrophage perturbations from tagged HEK293T interaction experiments. DDX3X associates with the NLRP3 NACHT region and supports inflammasome assembly in those conditions. The human ISS assignments remain ortholog inferences; no measured higher-order architecture, universal helicase requirement or short-product equivalence is asserted. PMID:28869602(https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28869602/), fractionation, imaging and mitochondrial translation experiments, supports a conditional mitochondrial association and translation effect without a resolved direct mitochondrial mechanism.

PMID:24965446(https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24965446/), Npro/DDX3 Results and stress-treatment Methods, uses sodium arsenate and reports redistribution/colocalization. These data do not demonstrate that DDX3X performs transport or retention of proteins in granules. GO:1903608 is currently obsolete because its historical usage confused colocalization with a process; both this ontology fact and the source-specific mechanistic limitation support the overannotation judgment.

Initiation-factor scope and additional public locators

PMID:22323517, original, Methods Purification of translation factors and Reconstitution of 48S and 80S initiation complexes, and Results/Figure 7F–G, distinguishes human-cell-purified FLAG-DDX3 from bacterial inclusion-body protein used only for quantification. With purified 40S, eIF3 and initiator tRNA on the HCV-derived reporter, added FLAG-DDX3 did not increase 48S assembly. Adding 60S and eIF5B (587–1220) produced more 80S complexes with FLAG-DDX3. The FLAG fraction lacked detectable eIF2/eIF3/eIF5 and ribosomal subunits and did not assemble complexes alone. This is a performed assembly contribution, supporting the auxiliary initiation-factor description; it is not just co-immunoprecipitation or necessity. The assay does not establish an ATPase requirement or the proposed physical bridge.

PMID:10074132, original, DOI 10.1128/JVI.73.4.2841-2853.1999, contains the NTPase-dNTPase activity analysis of His·CAP-Rf Methods, Figure 7 nucleotide-hydrolysis caption and Table 2 polynucleotide/substrate matrix used in this review. Selected indexed original passages were inspected; the normal publication cache remains abstract-only, direct publisher/BioC attempts failed, and figure pixels were not inspected. The human HuH-7 reporter increase is a positive expression outcome; its causal stage is not resolved into transcription versus RNA handling or translation by that observation alone.

PMID:29899501(https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5998047/), Results TRPV4 cation channel interacts with DDX3X RNA helicase, Figure 1d–g, reports a tagged DDX3X pool at the plasma membrane after removal of excessive cytosolic signal and reduced association after TRPV4 activation. This independently corroborates the compartment assigned to PMID:23413191(https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1231499); it does not recover that earlier study’s localization assay. The IRF3 quotation above remains here because the normal PMID:23478265 cache lacks the original passage; it is not copied into cache-validated YAML.

description: 'DDX3X is a DEAD-box RNA helicase that binds RNA and uses an ATP-dependent cycle to remodel short RNA duplexes. It promotes translation of selected mRNAs and supports formation of functional 80S initiation complexes through interactions with translation-initiation machinery. DDX3X also performs separable noncatalytic signaling roles: it helps recruit IRF3 to IKKε during antiviral interferon induction and stimulates casein kinase 1 in Wnt signaling. The protein shuttles between nucleus and cytoplasm and can enter stress granules and other conditional assemblies. Its cellular effects depend on transcript, stimulus and cell type. Pathogenic DDX3X variants are associated with neurodevelopmental disease.'

suggested_questions:
- question: Which RNA substrates and assay conditions explain the reported DNA unwinding and RNA annealing activities, and can the DNA result be independently reproduced given the 2026 correction and incomplete original data?
- question: Does DDX3X directly contact poly(A) tails in the export mRNP experiments, or do the observations reflect contact with other portions of polyadenylated transcripts?
- question: Which activities and cellular distributions distinguish the naturally occurring 646-residue product from the 662-residue product?
- question: Which molecular steps connect DDX3X to intrinsic apoptosis, mitochondrial translation and cadherin-associated neighborhoods in the source-specific contexts where those assignments remain uncertain?
suggested_experiments:
- description: Compare sequence-verified 662- and 646-residue products in matched RNA binding/unwinding, initiation-complex reconstitution and signaling assays, with expression and folding controls.
- description: Retest DNA unwinding with matched 5′- and 3′-tailed duplexes, tag-cleaved preparations and orthogonal product detection; separately test target-specific RNA annealing and poly(A)-tail contact.
